title: Development of Fedora Linux Distribution for RISC-V (RV64G) Architecture
problem: RISC-V systems lacking compressed instruction support (RV64G) lack mature Linux distribution support. The current software ecosystem has insufficient tooling and infrastructure for these systems.
motivation: Proper software infrastructure is essential for RISC-V ecosystem maturity and enabling adoption in HPC applications.
method: To create a complete Linux system for RISC-V processors, the approach systematically establishes the filesystem hierarchy (the directory structure Linux needs to run), develops a cross-compiler (a compiler that runs on standard computers but generates code for RISC-V), and uses it to bootstrap an initial system on the target platform. A native GCC compiler (one that compiles directly on RISC-V) is then installed on the bootstrapped system. Finally, a custom Python script automates the Koji build system (a tool for compiling and packaging software) to rebuild all necessary packages for the complete Linux environment.
key_novelty: A custom Python automation tool manages Koji builds to rebuild the entire Linux software ecosystem for RV64G.
contributions: Complete Fedora Linux distribution tailored for RV64G architecture
Integrated cross-compiler and native GCC toolchain
Koji build system integration for systematic package rebuilding
Python automation tool for build efficiency
limitations: Specific performance comparisons and benchmarks not discussed.
